title: Measured roadside-grass harvest performance in two Lincolnshire campaigns
license: CC BY 4.0, stated on the open-access article
source_location: Results §§3.1 and 3.4, pp. 6–7 of the article PDF

units_and_basis.moisture_percent: percent of fresh mass; reported approximately
units_and_basis.road_travel_speed_km_per_h: km per hour while traveling between road and harvest sites
units_and_basis.very_wet_harvest_speed_km_per_h: km per hour while harvesting under the source's qualitative very-wet condition
units_and_basis.harvester_capacity_t: tonnes of cut grass carried by the 2018 harvesting vehicle; source does not specify wet/dry basis

data_handling: Transcribed only values stated in Results §§3.1 and 3.4. Approximate source values are retained at their printed precision; unreported campaign-specific fields are blank, not inferred. No conversion or averaging was performed by GreenHub.
limitations: The 2016 value is a single test harvest; the authors note it was unusually high following warm and wet growing conditions.
The 2018 values are pilot averages during a season with an unusually cold spring and hot/dry summer.
No site-level distribution, replicate count, or measurement uncertainty is reported for the aggregate harvest results.
These are UK measurements and do not establish Dutch roadside yield, access, contracts, ecological retention, or GreenHub delivered feed.

The source's dry/very-wet harvest speeds are qualitative condition cases with no moisture threshold or speed distribution; road travel speed is not an in-field harvest speed. Vehicle capacity is not specified on a dry-mass basis.
Keep measured harvest yields separate from Table 5 regional supply scenarios, which apply the 2016 fresh-yield assumption to road-network areas.
